caption: Every teacher I know says the first salary disappears in a week. Did yours?

slides.title:
My first year
as a teacher
on R16 450 p/m
Living in Makhado
slides.body:
Female, 23
Single, lives with her parents
Job: Foundation phase teacher, first year
Net salary: R16 450 p/m

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My parents' bond contribution, my brother's varsity registration
slides.body: The first salary was never going to be only mine. I knew that on the way to the bank.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: The school is out of town, so I needed it before I earned it.

slides.title: Petrol
slides.includes: Daily drive to a rural school, 38 km each way
slides.body: Once a month the road to school is closed, and I go the long way.

slides.title: Student loan
slides.includes: Bank loan for my last two years of fees
slides.body: NSFAS didn't cover everything. I'll pay for another three years.

slides.title: Clothes and hair
slides.includes: Looking the part for Grade 2, hair every month, one dress
slides.body: I'm not proud of this line. Twenty seven children don't care what I wear.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries contribution, phone, funeral policy, stokvel, takeaways
slides.body: The teachers' stokvel is R800. It pays out in December and I've planned that money three times.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R16 450. It's the most money I've ever had and I've still run out by the 22nd.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it sorted my first full month into categories.

Black tax was the biggest line, and I wasn't surprised.

No bank login needed.
